headline: A lingering offshore low keeps showers and cool weather through Friday, then a mostly dry, chilly weekend and midweek follow.
summary: As of Wednesday evening, forecasters expect a cold pool of air high in the atmosphere (an upper-level low) to sit just offshore and barely move through Friday. That keeps western Washington unsettled, with scattered lowland showers and light Cascade snow. Highs Thursday and Friday should be in the low to mid 50s. Rain totals should trend down, and much of the area may stay somewhat dry between showers, though stray showers can't be ruled out. Wednesday's small chance (15 to 20%) of a thunderstorm was expected to fade sharply after sunset. The Cascades Winter Weather Advisory ended at 5 PM Wednesday. Cascade snow showers had faded a lot since the morning, and most of the snow fell in and around Mount Rainier. Over the weekend the low weakens and conditions turn drier, with highs around the mid 50s. Nights get colder, with lows in the low to mid 30s, and a few spots, especially in the Southwest Interior, could drop to the mid to upper 20s. A weak upper-level ridge (a zone of higher pressure aloft) should keep things likely dry into the middle of next week. Forecasters say the models agree the low weakens into the weekend, but the timing of any stray showers Thursday and Friday is less certain. Earlier in the day, forecasters had mentioned possible patchy morning fog early next week, but the evening discussion did not carry that forward.
changes: Earlier discussions emphasized a Cascade snow advisory, possible thunderstorms, and patchy fog Monday and Tuesday mornings. By evening the advisory had expired, snow had faded, and the fog mention was gone, leaving a drier, colder weekend outlook with some nights dropping to the mid to upper 20s.
